1.reason: Field lines show both direction (tangent) and relative strength (line density).

2.reason: Field at centre of a circular coil of N turns is B = mu0*N*I/(2r).

4.reason: Inducing current by a changing magnetic field is electromagnetic induction (Faraday).

6.reason: Fuse wire has low resistance and low melting point (melts on overload).

7.reason: A current-carrying solenoid produces a field pattern identical to a bar magnet.

8.reason: REVIEW: Domestic supply uses live, neutral and earth; among the options 'red, black, blue' is the closest standard set. Options (a) and (b) are identical (duplicate).

9.reason: REVIEW: tau = N B I A cos(30) = 20*2e-2*0.1*(0.20*1.00)*cos30 ~ 6.9e-3; sin form ~4e-3. Value does not match cleanly; closest given is 1.4e-3 N m. Best guess D.

10.reason: REVIEW: Current wire deflects a compass (Oersted); deflection direction depends on current direction not fully specified. Standard intended answer is towards left. Best guess D.

11.reason: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a field is given by Fleming's left-hand rule.

12.reason: A 15 A circuit is for high-power appliances such as geysers/heaters.

13.reason: A conductor along the loop axis: by symmetry the net force on the coaxial loop is zero.

14.reason: A coil of many circular turns wound on a former is a solenoid.

15.reason: Alnico is an alloy of Aluminium, Nickel and Cobalt (Al-Ni-Co).

17.reason: REVIEW: Right-hand thumb rule gives field direction; an A.C. generator uses Fleming's right-hand rule, not the thumb rule. Best guess A.

18.reason: REVIEW: Permanent magnets are made of steel, alnico and nipermag; tungsten steel is also used. Printed sub-options map (a)A and B,(b)A B and D,(c)A B and C,(d)A and D. Best guess C (1,2 and 3).

29.reason: REVIEW: By right-hand rule for current east->west, the field points north-to-south at the point directly below the wire. Best guess A.

31.reason: Earth wire=Green(iii); Dry cell=DC(ii); tightly packed helix=Solenoid(iv); temporary magnetism=Electromagnet(i). Matches option A. (a and c are duplicate options.)

32.reason: Like poles=Repel(iv); Unlike poles=Attract(i); Live=Red(iii); Neutral=Black(ii) = option C.

33.reason: Faraday=EM induction(B); Fleming=force on conductor(D); Maxwell=lines of force / corkscrew(A); Oersted=Electromagnetism(C) = option D.

34.reason: SI unit=Tesla(B); field inside solenoid=Uniform(D); compass needle=small bar magnet rotating freely(A); solenoid=temporary magnet(C). So 1-B,2-D,3-A,4-C = option C.

35.reason: Iron ore=Loadstone(A); flux=lines through surface(C); motor=electrical to mechanical(B); permanent magnet=Bar magnet(D) = option A.

36.reason: Dynamo works on electromagnetic principle(i); area around magnet=Magnetic field(iv); device mechanical->electrical=Generator(ii); Ampere=Magnetism(iii) = option C.

37.reason: The main switch disconnects both live and neutral wires.

38.reason: REVIEW: Earth's magnetic axis is inclined to the geographic axis; the value quoted in this text is 17 degrees. Best guess B.

39.reason: Inside a long solenoid the field is uniform, so field lines are straight and parallel.

40.reason: REVIEW: A changing magnetic field can induce current in a wire (A true); like poles repel (B true). Best guess C.

41.reason: Oersted first noticed the magnetic effect of current (A true); closeness of field lines indicates strength (B true) = C.

42.reason: A short circuit is live touching neutral (1) which causes current to abruptly increase (2); both apply -> Both A and B.

43.reason: REVIEW: (b),(c),(d) are correct properties of field lines; (a) is the garbled/incorrect statement. Best guess A.

44.reason: REVIEW: Overloading arises from too many appliances and a supply-voltage hike; live-neutral contact is short circuit. Printed intended answer 'All of these' (D). Best guess D.

45.reason: Parallel, equidistant field lines represent a UNIFORM (not zero) field, so (b) is incorrect.

46.reason: REVIEW: Field lines form closed loops (1 true); neutral ~zero voltage (2 true); DC heat loss less than AC (3 generally accepted true); fuse is not current-generating (4 false). True=1,2,3 -> 'A, B and C' = option D. Best guess D.

47.reason: REVIEW: Statement 1 (emerge from south) wrong, 2 (lines intersect) wrong, 3 (red=neutral) wrong - all three incorrect, so 'All of these'. Printed option labelled (a) 'D' = All of these. Best guess A.

48.reason: REVIEW: 'Thinner fuse = greater current capacity' (C) is wrong; 'capacity must be less than maximum current' (D) is wrong. So C and D are not correct = option C.

49.reason: Statement 1 is incorrect: the solenoid field pattern is the SAME as a bar magnet's, not different. So statement (1) is incorrect = option A.

50.reason: Statement 3 is incorrect: the solenoid field pattern is the SAME as a bar magnet, not different. So statement (3) is incorrect = option C.

51.reason: India AC is 50 Hz, so it changes direction every 1/100 s (reverses twice per cycle), not 1/50 s. So (d) is incorrect.

52.reason: REVIEW: Fuse=tin-lead alloy (1 true); switch on live wire (2 true); AC is not unidirectional (3 false); higher current gives stronger field (4 false). True=1,2 -> 'A and B', which is not offered cleanly; printed options ambiguous. Best guess A.

53.reason: Silver has the lowest resistivity (1.60e-8), so it is the best conductor for transmission lines.

54.reason: REVIEW: Mean force per electron f = B e v_d with I = n e A v_d; the given data yield ~1.2e-24 N order. Closest option is 12e-25 = 1.2e-24 N -> option A. Best guess A.
